test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A certain sum is invested at a simple interest rate of 12% per annum for a certain period of time. If the sum becomes four times the principal at the end of the period, what is the duration of the investment?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a sum to become n times its principal, the time duration T is given by:

T = [(n − 1) × 100] / R

Given: n = 4 (sum becomes 4 times), R = 12%

T = [(4 − 1) × 100] / 12

T = [3 × 100] / 12 = 300 / 12 = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = P

Amount (A) = 4P

Rate of Interest (R) = 12% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 
• 
 
 
 Principal (P)
 Amount (4P)
 

 Interest (SI) = 3P
 Rate = 12%
 Time = T years

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 4P − P = 3P

⇒ 3P = (P × 12 × T) / 100

⇒ 3 = (12 × T) / 100

⇒ 300 = 12 × T

⇒ T = 300 / 12

⇒ T = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period. SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Compound Interest Comparison

Unlike SI, Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods. A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Rule for sum doubling/tripling

For a sum to double (n=2), T = 100/R. For a sum to triple (n=3), T = 200/R under simple interest.</p
